typography.evidence: A typeface cannot be identified from pixels. Record the type ROLE (serif/sans, display/UI) in design-spec.json as interpretation.

density.evidence: A single presentation board does not reliably yield information density; it is a per-screen judgement. Record it in the spec.

paletteCandidates.note: Cluster centres over a board that includes photography and presentation background. Flat UI fields in the reference sit in a band around these, not exactly on them.

brand.basis: most saturated cluster weighted by share

reasons: the reference keeps its ground quiet and delegates colour to actions and state (saturation regime: mixed)
a light, near-neutral ground is the reference's own canvas
the reference rations its hue (saturation regime: mixed) — a full field would overstate it
one hue family dominates, so a committed field has a single colour to commit
a light ground lets a committed field read as an accent plane rather than the whole app
the reference canvas reads light, so inverting it to dark would not be faithful

recommendation.note: Scores rank the archetypes against measured properties only. They do not know the brief, the product category, or the client. A human may override — and the override must be recorded in directions.json.

principles.principle: Hue is rationed: colour is reserved for actions, selection and state; surfaces stay neutral.
One hue family does all the accent work, so "this colour means tappable / current" is learnable in one screen.
principles.basis: 97.6% of coloured pixels in the modal hue family (single-hue>=45%)

principles.principle: Ground is light: hierarchy starts from a light canvas.
Numeric and state grammar must be identical on every screen (prices, totals, timestamps, statuses).

notToCopy: Marketing-only composition: a presentation board shows a hero and a few cards; it does not show empty, loading, error or long-list states. Those must be designed, not inferred.
Missing application states: several reference kits ship zero error states and zero empty states. Their absence is a gap in the reference, not a design decision to honour.
Photography as the quality carrier: if the reference leans on product photography, substituting illustrations caps the ceiling — declare the substitution instead of pretending it matches.
Screenshot-specific artefacts: off-screen steppers, clipped frames and placeholder personas in the source board are not design intent.
Layout copying: the reference shows one product's information architecture. Copying its layout imports its product decisions, which may contradict the brief.
